evidence.text:
The reported futures orders growth is not necessarily indicative of our expectation of revenue growth during this period. This is due to year-over-year changes in shipment timing, changes in the mix of orders between futures and at-once orders and because the fulfillment of certain orders may fall outside of the schedule noted above. In addition, exchange rate fluctuations as well as differing levels of order cancellations, discounts and returns can cause differences in the comparisons between futures orders and actual revenues. Moreover, a portion of our revenue is not derived from futures orders, including sales of at-once and closeout NIKE Brand footwear and apparel, sales of NIKE Brand equipment, sales from our DTC operations and sales from Converse, NIKE Golf and Hurley. 
 Gross Margin

attrs.management_says: Futures orders for Jun-Nov 2015 delivery were +2% reported (+13% currency-neutral), but shipment timing, order mix, and cancellations can cause differences vs. actual revenue (E36, E37).
attrs.numbers_show: Actual FY2015 revenue grew 10.1% with steady quarterly growth and no anomalous quarter-end receivables spikes (E25, E27-E30). The futures orders signal is directionally consistent but not precise, as management cautioned.

attrs.management_says: Futures orders not necessarily indicative of revenue due to shipment timing, mix changes between futures/at-once orders, cancellations, discounts, returns (E37).
attrs.numbers_show: Quarterly AR peaked in Q1 ($3,587M) then declined each quarter to $3,358M while revenue remained elevated (E27-E30). Full-year AR fell despite revenue growth, DSO improved steadily — not a pattern of temporary timing inflation.

attrs.management_says: Futures orders not necessarily indicative of revenue due to shipment timing, mix changes, cancellations (E37).
attrs.numbers_show: Quarter-end receivables grew slower than revenue in Q1 (+11.8% vs +14.5%) and Q2 (+7.8% vs +14.8%), then fell in Q3 (-1.8% vs +7.0%) and Q4 (-2.2% vs +4.8%) while DSO improved each quarter (E27-E30).

attrs.reason: Reported futures orders growth (13% currency-neutral, E36) and actual revenue growth (10.1%, E13 vs E1) are directionally consistent, and quarterly revenue shows steady growth with no receivables spikes (E27-E30), corroborating management's caution that futures orders are not precise predictors due to timing, mix, and cancellations (E37).

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: Management explicitly cautioned that futures orders are not precise predictors of revenue due to shipment timing, order mix changes, and cancellations (E37). The actual FY2015 revenue growth of 10.1% (E13 vs E1) with steady quarterly growth and no quarter-end receivables spikes (E27-E30) is directionally consistent with the currency-neutral futures orders growth of 13% (E36), and the absence of anomalous receivables buildup argues against channel stuffing.

attrs.reason: Management's statement (E37) is a disclaimer about futures orders as a forward-looking indicator, not a causal explanation for the fiscal 2015 receivables pattern. The numbers (E27-E30) show a steady DSO improvement and declining AR amid rising revenue, but they do not contradict the disclaimer because the disclaimer does not assert a specific receivables pattern. Since the statement is not a causal claim about the observed pattern, it cannot be tested as fitting or not fitting; it is unverified.
